lead.en: Phaya Thai khet is best read as three districts in one. Along Phahonyothin, Ari's Soi 1-7 grid pairs mid-rise condos with cafe-filled quiet sois, while Saphan Khwai two stops north concentrates shops, apartments and a junction that police close for major events. Between them, Pradiphat still carries its military-institutional character, and along Vibhavadi the Army Club and stadium occupy the largest green block - land you can see but not freely use. Rents reflect the split: portal asks from the 12,000s in older stock to 35,000+ in Ari's newer buildings.

strengths.en: Three BTS stations inside the khet plus the ARL interchange one stop south - the district's core transit promise
Ari's walkable cafe sois one soi off the arterial, with street-food-priced eating on Soi Phahonyothin 7
Deep everyday healthcare: five private/military hospitals in-district plus Phramongkutklao across the boundary
Wide rent ladder (roughly 12,000-45,000 THB asking) letting budget and mid-market renters live within walking distance of the same line

tradeoffs.en: Phahonyothin rush-hour congestion and the Saphan Khwai junction chokepoint, which police advise avoiding city-wide on big-event days
Public green is pocket-scale: BMA's named parks here are expressway-margin leftovers of ~1-2 ha, while the big green is restricted military land
Flood exposure on some low sois in heavy rain, per the district guide's own cons list
Evening quiet: the area is cafe-daytime oriented and 'sleepy' after dark for those wanting nightlife

dayNight.en: Weekday mornings: school and office flows concentrate on Phahonyothin; Saphan Khwai junction backs up toward the sois
Daytime: Ari's cafes and the PRD garden at the end of Soi Ari Samphan absorb the district's leisure foot traffic
Event days: junction-level closures around GSB head office can cut the crossing for a full day (06:00-18:00 advisories)
Evenings: commercial energy drains; the guide describes Ari as sleepier than Sukhumvit-side districts

variation.en: Ari (Soi Ari 1-7, Ari Samphan): cafe-residential, the guide's most expensive and most walkable band
Saphan Khwai: denser, 'grittier, more local', cheapest stock, district's most concentrated population
Pradiphat-Sanam Pao: military plots between residential conversions; history visible in street fabric
Vibhavadi edge: Army Club/stadium, Channel 5, Veterans' Hospital - green without public access
Sam Sen Nai-Inthamara: plain townhouse/apartment grid, few named amenities, no BMA park on its own streets

fit.en: Fit: cafe-culture workers and remote workers priced out of Thonglor/Asoke who want calm sois near BTS
Fit: budget renters targeting Saphan Khwai's apartment stock who work locally or tolerate junction traffic
Poor fit: nightlife-first residents and anyone whose commute crosses town daily (30+ min to Silom/Sathorn per the guide)
Poor fit: households that need daily park access - the khet's public parks are pocket-scale and unevenly placed
Watch item: monsoon-season flooding on specific low sois; ask street-by-street, not district-wide

uncertainties: Green 9 basis unresolved: the 14.8 ha could not be decomposed (OSM queries blocked); the Army compound is the only candidate large enough, and it is not public parkland [phaya-thai-c06, c07]
Safety 8 untested: no systematic crime statistic found; 2024-2026 news search returned only scattered, poorly-locatable incidents [phaya-thai-c14]
App rent reference sits above district-wide portal averages for 2-beds and at the low end for Ari 1-beds; sample definitions differ (portal listings vs editorial estimate) [phaya-thai-c11]

App counts (23 temples, 8 markets, 1,302 food places) could not be matched to named sources; EN/TH wiki name only Wat Phai Tan as the khet's temple, and no wet market was verifiable [phaya-thai-c01 limitations, Q07]
Suan Phaya Thai Phirom's side of the Ratchathewi boundary is ambiguous between BMA and third-party maps [phaya-thai-c07]

limitations: app baseline (67,388 in 2020) not independently located in a published table; consistent in magnitude with the sourced snapshots
station-footprint straddling a boundary line cannot be fully excluded from wiki text alone; both district and station articles agree on Ratchathewi
Chatuchak park placement rests on the boundary line plus common knowledge of those parks' locations; not verified by a dedicated park source in this run
Vachirabenjatas Park '450 rai' figure seen only in a search snippet and not used here

Conflict noted 2026-11-07: a point-in-polygon test against the app's own khet polygon (geometry.json) places the Victory Monument roundabout (~13.7699, 100.5350) INSIDE the phaya-thai khet, while the source attributes it to Ratchathewi - the monument sits at the boundary; treat its attribution as conflicting.
street address, capacity and golf/driving-range operation come from snippet-level sources (search result and Facebook page info), not opened pages
no source found quantifying the compound's area in hectares
composition of the 14.8 ha could not be decomposed: Overpass/OSM queries failed from this environment (HTTP 406/timeout/malformed) and Greener pages give no per-park areas
boundary side of Suan Phaya Thai Phirom is ambiguous (BMA lists it under the khet; Moovit labels it Ratchathewi; OSM point is near the boundary)
Suan Ari Samphan details (PRD garden, cafes inside) rest on snippet-level search results corroborating the Greener listing
specific cafe named from a snippet-level source only
guide is property-audience content

single-source historical narrative (Thai wiki road article); plausible but not independently corroborated in this run
